condition: odontogenic Ludwig submandibular space infection presenting with rapidly progressive indurated submandibular swelling
level_rationale: Fast-spreading hard swelling under the jaw today in a 34-year-old man who cracked a lower molar 4 days ago indicates suspected odontogenic submandibular deep-space infection (Ludwig angina) with airway risk requiring immediate emergency hospital evaluation, whereas feeling a sharp rough edge on that cracked tooth today without submandibular swelling warrants specialist dental restoration by a dentist.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + causal belief-addition clause (-att) + same-tooth uncomplicated rough-molar-edge dental control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (34-year-old man, cracked lower molar 4 days ago, and fast-spreading hard swelling under the jaw today) with a 2-word span difference (14 vs 16 words) and 8 shared trailing tokens ('today so I need to go to the'). Swapping only f3 to feeling a sharp rough edge on that cracked tooth stays inside the exact same cracked-molar case while shifting care from emergency hospital airway evaluation (level 4) to dental restoration by a dentist (level 3) with zero stated negatives.
